title: 1. Resolve same-placement tape divergence before branching traces
hypothesis: Reconstructing the complete vectorized reset context prevents the state drift that invalidates same-placement action-tape replay.

prediction.rationale: Compare full-context replay with target-only same-placement replay using the frozen episode-success rule. A 0.25 gain would make scene reconstruction a material prerequisite for counterfactual traces; require a paired interval excluding zero. Unlike D-037, this tests recording fidelity on the recorded cases, not open-loop generalization to new placements.

protocol.command: gpu run 'source ~/IsaacLab/source_env.sh && python scripts/audit_expert_actions.py --config config/pen_spin_plateau_repair.yaml --protocol scene_context_replay'
code_changes: scripts/audit_expert_actions.py: add the declared --protocol mode, reusing the validated Isaac runner rather than the legacy smoke rollout.

config/pen_spin_plateau_repair.yaml: freeze 16 Stage-3 cases; record the qualified expert in a 16-lane scene, then replay each target tape in the reconstructed whole scene and in a target-only scene. Execute identical already-scaled actions, use the existing episode-success rule, and record initial-state hashes and first observation divergence.
Record every lane's reset seed, initialization tensors, lane order, controller initialization and reset schedule; target-only replay must restore the target's recorded initial state.
config/manifests/pen_spin_stage3_replay_audit_s4300.yaml: add and freeze before execution; register the seed in config/experiment_seed_ledger.jsonl.
RESEARCH_HANDOFF.md: document whether exact self-replay is qualified, without revising D-037's cross-placement conclusion.

falsified_by: The paired interval's upper bound is below +0.25; an interval including zero is inconclusive about a directional difference. Failure of full-context replay itself leaves faithful counterfactual branching unqualified.
direction: Continue researching the single-step exploration pipeline with plateau-triggered trace repair, extended to pen spinning on the Shadow Hand (Isaac Lab Isaac-ShadowHandSpin-Stage{1,2,3}-Direct-v0, vendored in lares/envs/isaac_pen_spin; 157-d full obs, 20-d action, 60 Hz, 360-step episodes). Expert demonstrations: first try a hand-written scripted spinning controller; also search online for an existing trained pen-spinning policy; if neither qualifies, train an RL expert (rsl_rl PPO on the box). No budget ceiling on GPU hours or LLM calls. Known gaps to turn into questions: the env's spin_rate is roll about the pen's own long axis (not end-over-end twirl), success is per step with no episode rule, and the pipeline (manifests, obs schema, runner, records) is MetaWorld-only today. Debug issues, improve the pipeline, and turn unexpected findings into concrete research questions; document results and limitations.

advisor.reasoning: This is the cheapest prerequisite for trustworthy counterfactual traces, and it tests recording fidelity rather than duplicating D-037's cross-placement generalization result. Its weakest point is that improved success does not establish faithful replay, while reconstructing a separate 16-lane scene for every target would exceed the stated 48-episode budget. Keep this a 48-simulator-episode, zero-LLM-call audit using free seed 4300.
suggested_changes: Keep the paired_success_difference prediction of an increase of at least 0.25 against target-only same-placement replay and its existing falsified_by, but separate that contrast from downstream replay qualification. Require bit-identical full observation trajectories and identical frozen-rule outcomes for all 16 full-context self-replays; any mismatch leaves branching unqualified regardless of the success contrast.

In scripts/audit_expert_actions.py and config/pen_spin_plateau_repair.yaml, explicitly record and replay all 16 lanes' action tapes and reset schedules together, preserving lane order, initialization, RNG state and timing, with already-scaled actions applied exactly once.

Freeze the execution schedule as one 16-lane recording, one simultaneous 16-lane full-context replay, and 16 single-lane target-only replays: 48 simulator lane-episodes total. Do not silently substitute 16 separate full-scene reconstructions, which would raise the total to 288 lane-episodes.

implementer.reasoning: Branching does not need open-loop action-tape replay. D-034 and the R-044/R-047 reproducibility controls show that one manifest run in a fresh Isaac process under the same closed-loop controller is bit-identical across processes (0 diverged envs, 0 flips, twice). A branch at step t is therefore obtained by re-running the same manifest batch in a fresh process with a controller that switches from learner to expert at a per-case step t: the prefix is the same closed-loop computation, so it reproduces exactly without recording or replaying any tape. Tape replay fidelity is a different question (D-037 already shows open-loop replay is not a usable controller) and qualifying it would spend a protocol on a mechanism nothing downstream needs. R-051 can carry its own qualification gate: an unchanged-learner process that must be bit-identical to the donor run before any takeover is interpreted.

advisor.reasoning: I accept the implementer's argument: closed-loop prefix re-execution with its own reproducibility gate removes tape fidelity as a prerequisite for R-051. This audit's predicted paired_success_difference increase of at least 0.25 against target-only same-placement replay would not itself establish faithful trajectories; its falsified_by remains an interval upper bound below +0.25. Reject the 48-episode, zero-LLM-call spend because no current downstream experiment requires this mechanism. Reconsider only if a downstream protocol requires action-tape replay, or closed-loop reconstruction fails for a reason this audit could isolate.

implementer.reasoning: Agree with round 2: no downstream protocol needs tape replay; closed-loop re-execution with its own gate replaces it.
